concepts.name: Story elements
concepts.summary: Name and recognise the core parts of a story: character, setting, conflict, plot and ending.

concepts.name: Point of view basics
concepts.summary: Distinguish first-person and third-person narration and describe how each changes what the reader knows.

concepts.name: Concrete versus abstract language
concepts.summary: Understand why specific, concrete nouns and verbs create clearer images than vague abstractions.

concepts.name: Sensory detail
concepts.summary: Explain how details of sight, sound, smell, taste and touch make a scene feel real to the reader.

concepts.name: Show versus tell
concepts.summary: Understand the difference between stating an emotion or fact and conveying it through action, detail and dialogue.

concepts.name: Simile and metaphor
concepts.summary: Recall and identify similes and metaphors as comparisons that describe one thing in terms of another.

concepts.name: Freewriting habit
concepts.summary: Understand that writing a rough first draft without self-editing generates raw material to refine later.

misconceptions.text: Good writing should come out polished on the first try.
Showing means never stating anything directly.
Using more adjectives and fancy words always makes description better.

concepts.name: Character desire and flaw
concepts.summary: Give a character a concrete want and a limiting flaw that drive their choices on the page.

concepts.name: Scene construction
concepts.summary: Write a scene with a clear setting, a character who wants something, an obstacle and a shift by the end.

concepts.name: Dialogue that reveals
concepts.summary: Write dialogue that sounds natural, carries subtext and reveals character, with correct punctuation and tags.

concepts.name: Plot structure arc
concepts.summary: Explain how setup, rising action, climax and resolution shape a short story's progression.

concepts.name: Setting as atmosphere
concepts.summary: Use selected details of place and weather to establish mood rather than listing everything visible.

concepts.name: Imagery in poetry
concepts.summary: Write short poems built on fresh, concrete images instead of stated feelings.

concepts.name: Line breaks and rhythm
concepts.summary: Use line breaks, stress and sound patterns such as alliteration to control pace and emphasis in a poem.

concepts.name: Self-editing pass
concepts.summary: Reread a draft to cut filler, fix clichés and tighten sentences.

misconceptions.text: Dialogue should copy real speech exactly, including every filler word and pleasantry.
Every story needs a big dramatic event or twist to work.
A poem must rhyme to be a poem.

concepts.name: Point of view control
concepts.summary: Choose a viewpoint and maintain consistent narrative distance, avoiding head-hopping and knowledge the narrator lacks.

concepts.name: Subtext and implication
concepts.summary: Analyse and craft passages where the meaning lies beneath what characters say or do.

concepts.name: Pacing and scene-summary balance
concepts.summary: Decide when to dramatise in scene and when to compress in summary to control tempo.

concepts.name: Character arc and change
concepts.summary: Analyse how events pressure a character's belief so they change, or fail to change, across a story.

concepts.name: Theme through motif
concepts.summary: Develop theme implicitly through recurring images, objects and patterns rather than stated morals.

concepts.name: Poetic form and device
concepts.summary: Apply forms and devices such as free verse, enjambment, volta and repetition deliberately to serve meaning.

concepts.name: Structured revision
concepts.summary: Revise in layers, from structure and character to paragraph and word level, diagnosing what each draft needs.

concepts.name: Giving and using feedback
concepts.summary: Analyse peer critique to separate the reader's symptoms from proposed fixes and decide what to act on.

misconceptions.text: Revision means correcting typos and grammar.
Theme is a moral the story should state clearly at the end.
Every piece of feedback must be followed to improve the work.

concepts.name: Distinctive voice
concepts.summary: Evaluate how diction, syntax, rhythm and attitude combine into a voice, and tune it to the piece.

concepts.name: Unreliable and layered narration
concepts.summary: Analyse how gaps between narrator and reader knowledge create irony and tension.

concepts.name: Structural experiment
concepts.summary: Judge when nonlinear, braided or fragmentary structures serve a story's meaning and when they distract.

concepts.name: Sound and syntax control
concepts.summary: Analyse and shape sentence length, cadence and sound to produce effect in prose and poetry.

concepts.name: Genre conventions and subversion
concepts.summary: Evaluate how a genre's conventions shape reader expectation and when to honour or subvert them.

concepts.name: Personal prose craft
concepts.summary: Evaluate how reflection, selection and honesty turn lived experience into shaped narrative with a larger point.

concepts.name: Critical reading as a writer
concepts.summary: Analyse published work to identify techniques and judge which are worth adapting.

misconceptions.text: Voice is a quirky style you add on top, such as slang or odd punctuation.
Experimental structure automatically makes writing more original.
Personal writing only needs to be true to events, not shaped like a story.

concepts.name: Original aesthetic vision
concepts.summary: Develop a coherent personal aesthetic and obsessions that unify a body of work.

concepts.name: Form invention and hybridity
concepts.summary: Create new or hybrid forms that fuse prose, poetry and other modes so form carries meaning.

concepts.name: Evaluating craft decisions
concepts.summary: Judge the trade-offs of craft choices against the intended effect and defend them.

concepts.name: Tradition and intertextuality
concepts.summary: Evaluate how a work converses with earlier texts and movements, using influence without imitation.

concepts.name: Ethics of representation
concepts.summary: Weigh the ethical and artistic consequences of depicting real people, other cultures and trauma.

concepts.name: Sustained long-form architecture
concepts.summary: Design the architecture of a collection, novella or sequence so pieces build cumulative meaning.

concepts.name: Mentoring and editorial judgement
concepts.summary: Assess others' drafts and guide revision toward the writer's own aims rather than imposing taste.

misconceptions.text: Originality means avoiding all influence and convention.
Breaking formal rules is always a sign of artistic mastery.
A collection is simply the best individual pieces gathered in any order.
